entries.content: God (a-4) Heb. Elohim, the plural of Eloah, 'the Supreme'. It is Deity in the absolute sense. Elohim will, in the text, appear only in the name of Jehovah Elohim; moreover, when Elohim following immediately on Jehovah has a grammatical adjunct, its place will be taken by the English word 'God'. see Gen. 9.26 and 24.7. Other Hebrew divine names translated as 'God' will be indicated as follows. Eloah +God; El, (meaning 'The Mighty,' see Gen. 14.18), *God. For the meaning of Jehovah, (Heb. Yahveh, or Yehveh), the ever-existing One, see Ex. 3.14,15; Isa. 40.28. For Jah, the existing One objectively, see Ex. 15.2; Ps. 68.4. The name seems to express absolute rather than continuous existence. For Adonai (a name of God, not merely a title), translated 'Lord', see Ezek. 2.4.
monsters, (b-7) The word applies to rivers as well as to the sea, and is also used for crocodiles, serpents. see Ex. 7.9.
Man (d-4) The Adam, Man, as a race. It will be spelled with a capital, to avoid repetition of the note.
moveth (e-42) Or 'creepeth;' and so elsewhere. Ch. 8.17,19.
histories (g-4) Lit. 'generations.' the word implies 'origin' and occurs in chs. 5.1; 6.9; 10.1,32; 11.10,27; 25.12,13,19; 36.1,9; 37.2. Elohim (h-20) See ch. 1.1.
grew; (i-21) Or 'no shrub ... was yet in the earth and no herb ... had yet grown.'
bdellium (c-9) A fragrant resin. as generally understood. onyx (d-12) Or 'beryl.'
Hiddekel. (e-9) i.e. Tigris. Asshur. (f-17) Or 'flows before Assyria.'
eat; (g-16) Lit. 'eating thou shalt eat.' an idiom constantly occurring, as again in ver. 17, 'dying thou shalt die.'
Woman, (i-21) Ishshah. man. (k-29) Ish. so husband ch. 3.6,16.
Abel. (b-7) Heb. Hebel, a breath (Job 7.16); or 'vanity' (Ps.144.4). shepherd, (c-12) Lit. 'herdsman of small cattle.' husbandman. (d-17) Lit. 'worked the ground.'
time (e-5) Lit. 'at the end of days.' offering (f-20) Lit. 'gift,' minchah. so vers. 4,5; elsewhere translated 'oblation.' See Lev. 2.1.

confidence]? (g-12) See Job 11.15. Or possibly, 'shalt thou not be accepted.' But I should question 'accepted,' the rather as nasa is used for it here. Lit. 'is there not a lifting up?' sin (h-19) Or 'a sin-offering,' Heb. chattath the word having both senses. see Note b Lev. 5.1. Also 'punishment.' see Note Zech. 14.19.
borne. (i-13) Or 'Mine iniquity (Heb.gahvon) is too great to be forgiven.' See Note Lam. 4.6.
Nod, (l-16) Flight, wandering. see ver. 12, where it is translated 'fugitive.'
of (a-14) Or 'the instructor of every worker in.' brass (b-15) Or 'bronze.' so always. Naamah. (c-24) Charming.
bruise. (d-35) Or 'to my wounding,' 'to my bruising.'
Enosh. (f-16) Man, as weak, mortal, Ps. 8.4; 103.15. on (g-22) Or 'to call themselves by,' but see chs. 12.8; 13.4; 21.33; 26.25.
Shem, (b-11) Name, renown. Ham, (c-12) Black. Japheth. (d-14) Spreading, enlargement.
mankind (e-7) Or 'Man;' and so vers. 2.4, 'men.' See Note to chs. 1.27; 3.12 and cf. ch. 7.21, &c. earth, (f-13) Lit. 'ground.'
with (g-10) Or 'plead in (or amongst) men.' 'strive in.' Many read 'plead with men in their wandering (or erring), he is flesh.'
renown. (h-43) Or 'the name,' i.e. who had a peculiar and known name on the earth. Heroes is Gibbor in Heb., meaning 'mighty men.'
destroy (k-6) Lit. 'blot,' or 'wipe out.' so ch. 7.4,23.
history (l-4) Lit. 'these are the generations.' See ch. 2.4. generations. (m-15) Refers to the circle in which Noah moved i.e. his contemporaries, as ch. 7.1; and could read 'in his times.'
life, (b-10) Lit. 'breath of spirit of life.'
retiring; (c-9) Lit. 'returned from the earth going and returning.'
I (e-2) Or '... earth, and the bow ... cloud, that I.'
Japheth, (c-4) See ch. 5.32. his (d-18) Or 'their,' i.e. Japheth's.
Cush, (g-6) These names are given later to countries, i.e. Ethiopia, Egypt, Libya.
out (k-5) Or 'he went to.' Asshur, (l-6) Assyria. so ver. 22.
from (f-9) Or 'started for.' Lit. 'pulled up their tent-pegs.'
south. (b-10) Negeb, 'south country.' name for the region of Canaan (Judah) bordering on the desert.
south. (b-23) Negeb, 'south country.' name for the region of Canaan (Judah) bordering on the desert.

plain (a-11) 'Circle.' used for the plain at the mouth of the Jordan, most of which was afterwards covered by the Salt sea. Ch. 14.3. Sodom (b-24) Burning. Gomorrah; (c-26) Submersion. Zoar. (d-41) Zor, or Zar, in Egypt. not Bela, ch. 14.2,8.
Shaveh-Kirjathaim, (f-30) Or 'in the plain of Kirjathaim.'
El-Paran, (g-9) Or 'to the terebinth of Paran.'
Hebrew. (a-11) Most explain, from across the Euphrates; but it might be derived from Eber. See ch. 10.21. allies. (b-35) Lit 'masters of covenant.'
Melchisedec (c-2) King of righteousness. *God. (d-19) El Elyon. El itself means 'The Mighty;' Elyon is habitually represented by 'Most High.' See Note to Gen. 1.1 also Deut. 32.8.
*God, (d-14) El Elyon. El itself means 'The Mighty;' Elyon is habitually represented by 'Most High.' See Note to Gen. 1.1 also Deut. 32.8.
*God, (d-7) El Elyon. El itself means 'The Mighty;' Elyon is habitually represented by 'Most High.' See Note to Gen. 1.1 also Deut. 32.8.
*God, (d-20) El Elyon. El itself means 'The Mighty;' Elyon is habitually represented by 'Most High.' See Note to Gen. 1.1 also Deut. 32.8.
Lord (e-4) Adonai, plural of Adon. 'Lord' will usually represent this word. go (f-13) Or 'depart.' steward (g-17) Lit. 'son of possession.' Eliezer (h-23) El is my help.
house (i-18) i.e. one of his domestics.
serve (a-25) Or 'be in bondage to.' so always of men.
that (b-16) Or 'gone down, it was dark, and.'
made (c-6) Lit. 'cut,' the regular idiom. river (d-21) Some read 'torrent.'
himself, (b-18) Lit. 'of the being seen,' or 'of the vision.'
Beer-lahai-roi. (c-6) Well of the Living who was seen (or 'who reveals himself').
Almighty (d-19) Shaddai plural of Shad, power. Isa. 13.6; Joel 1.15 may give its force. 'Almighty' will always represent Shaddai; 'the Almighty God' is El Shaddai.
Abram, (f-9) See ch. 11.26. Abraham; (g-15) Father of a multitude.
stranger (h-32) Or 'foreigner.' so ver. 27; Ex. 12.43; Lev. 22.25, &c.
standing (b-13) Lit. 'stationed themselves' as ch. 28.13; Ex. 17.9; not simply 'standing' as ch. 19.27 (see Note, John 1.26).
will (b-7) Or 'I have known him, in order that he may.'
place. (a-47) i.e. the ground before the city-gates.
quarter. (b-29) Lit. 'from the end,' with the force of 'to the end,' 'extremity;' see ch. 47.2,21.
be (c-18) The force is, 'again and again.' see ch. 31.15.
married (d-12) Or 'were to marry;' lit. 'the takers of.'
present, (e-21) Lit. 'are found.' iniquity (f-27) Or 'punishment.' See Zech. 14.19.
reproved. (a-42) Or 'the matter has been set right,' or 'thou art set right' -- each of these senses is possible.
not (a-12) Lit. 'If thou shalt,' a strong Hebrew expression meaning 'Thou shalt not.'
Beer-sheba, (b-6) Well of the oath, or seven. see ch. 26.33.
tamarisk (a-5) Or 'a grove.' *God. (b-18) El Olam see Isa. 40.28; Dan. 12.7; Mic. 5.2.
worship, (d-23) Lit. 'bow down.' so always. come (e-25) Lit. 'we will come.' See Heb. 11.19.
saith (h-7) The Hebrew word introduces an oracular discourse; cf. Num. 24.3,4,15,16. As 'He hath said,' Jer. 23.31.
themselves, (i-13) Or 'shall be blessed.' so ch. 26.4.
Aram-naharaim, (b-32) Syria of the two rivers.
stand (c-3) Same as word in ch. 18.2.
ring, (a-18) Nose-ring. see ver. 47; elsewhere also 'earring,' as ch. 35.4. shekel (b-22) Beka, as Ex. 38.26.
means (e-6) A strong obligation by oath, as Num. 14.28.
oath, (f-8) An oath with imprecation, as ch. 26.28.
way (b-24) Lit. 'in a way of truth.'
from (c-6) Lit. 'came from coming to.' Beer-lahai-roi; (d-7) See ch. 16.14.
settled (b-19) Or 'died.' Lit. 'fell;' and see ch. 16.12.
time, (h-12) Lit. 'when the days there were prolonged to him.'
valley (c-11) Elsewhere 'torrent;' it is a valley in which a torrent runs. see ch. 32.23.
company (b-19) Lit. 'congregation;' and so chs. 35.11; 48.4. See Ex. 12.6.
God. (b-17) Lit. 'Jehovah shall be to me for God.'
well? (d-8) Lit. 'Has he peace?' well; (e-14) Lit. 'Peace.'
Dinah. (g-11) Connected in meaning with Dan.
hereafter, (a-8) Lit. 'on the day of to-morrow.' face. (b-17) Or 'for it will come before thee with my wages.'
previously. (d-16) Lit. 'yesterday [and] the day before;' and so often.
previously; (d-17) Lit. 'yesterday [and] the day before;' and so often.
deceived (b-3) Lit. 'stole the heart of.' so ver. 26.
hand (c-9) Lit. 'my hand is as (serves for) God (El).'
Jegar-sahadutha, (c-5) Galeed. (c-10) The one is Aramaic, the other Hebrew. both meaning, 'Heap of witness.'
troops. (c-36) Lit. 'camps.' see v. 2. for (e-6) Lit. 'smaller than.' faithfulness (f-13) Lit. 'truth.'
joint (c-15) joint (c-21) The hollow of the joint.
Israel; (d-13) Wrestler, or prince of God. wrestled (e-17) Some, 'acted as a prince.'
joint (c-16) The hollow of the joint.
portion (d-5) Or 'allotment.' kesitahs. (e-28) Kesitah, a weight of precious metal. Supposed value about four shekels.
*God. (d-10) El-Shaddai. See ch 17.1. company (e-19) Or 'multitude' or 'assembly.'
up (f-4) Same Heb. word as 'standing' in ch. 18.2.
Benoni; (g-21) Son of my affliction. Benjamin. (h-27) Son of the right hand.
Migdal-Eder. (i-13) Tower of flocks. See Mic. 4.8.
chiefs (a-4) Heads of clans or families.
fed (c-12) Or 'was tending.' with (d-23) Or 'he was as a youth with.' them. (e-47) Or 'their evil discourse.'
colours. (f-26) Or 'a coat with sleeves;' and so vers. 23,32.
tragacanth, (d-29) A kind of gum. ladanum (e-33) An aromatic gum.
Sheol (a-31) Sheol. the 'hades' of the New Testament. see Ps. 6.5, and Note at Matt. 11.23.
chamberlain (b-11) See 1 Sam. 8.15. Pharaoh, (c-13) 'Pharaoh,' the title of the Egyptian kings.
lace, (a-17) Or chain by which the signet hung from the neck. so ver. 25.
prostitute (b-13) Strictly 'a woman consecrated [to the idol Astarte].'
man; (e-11) Or 'a man that caused prosperity.'
head (c-10) i.e. release him from the dungeon -- so 2 Kings 25.27.
years, (a-12) Lit. 'two years of days.' river. (b-22) The Nile.
scribes (c-22) i.e. Hieroglyphists. versed in so-called sacred writing -- hieroglyphics.
God (b-20) Or 'the spirit of the gods.'
byssus, (d-22) Fine Egyptian cotton or linen, see Ex. 25.4 and 39.28
Zaphnath-paaneah, (f-6) In Egyptian, 'Saviour of the world,' or 'Sustainer of life.' In Hebrew, 'Revealer of secrets.'
places (f-24) Or 'unfortified places.' lit. 'nakedness;' and so in ver. 12.

sack (c-7) Lit. 'sackcloth.' inn, (d-15) Caravanserai. so Ex. 4.24, &c. sack. (e-29) Or 'bag;' the other occurrences of the word in the chap. represent a different Hebrew word, relating to the material. See Note c.
sack. (e-20) Or 'bag;' the other occurrences of the word in the chap. represent a different Hebrew word, relating to the material. See Note c.
in (c-20) Lit. 'the celebrity of.' tragacanth (d-40) ladanum, (d-42) See ch. 37.25.
sacks, (e-21) 'Bag.' same as ch. 42.27,28, Note e; and so vers. 18,21,22,23; and ch. 44.1,2,8,11,12.
welfare, (b-7) Lit. 'of peace.' well (c-13) Lit. 'has your father peace?'
thing! (b-25) Lit. 'according to this word,' or 'thing.'
life, (a-28) Or 'his soul is knit with his soul.' see 1 Sam. 18.1.
yourselves, (e-11) Lit. 'let it not be an occasion of anger in your eyes.'
good (b-18) Or 'the best,' of soil or goods.
seventy. (a-29) Acts 7.14 is according to the LXX.
head. (a-18) Heb. 11.21 is according to the LXX. 'the top of his staff.'
land! (c-41) Or 'earth.' see Note 1 Sam. 2.8 and Matt. 5.5.
Impetuous (a-1) In the sense of the impetuosity of lust. Lit. 'bubbling up.'
swords. (b-10) The sense of the Hebrew word is doubtful.
assembly; (c-15) Or 'company' as ch. 28.3. oxen. (d-28) Some read 'pulled down a wall.'
thee; (e-10) Paronomasia, yehudah yoduca; Judah and praise. see ch. 29.35.
scepter (f-2) Or 'the staff [of the tribe].' lawgiver (g-10) Or 'sceptre' or 'staff of command.' see Num. 21.18. obedience (h-24) Many take it as 'gathering.'
judge (l-3) Paronomasia, Dan yadin; Dan and judge. see ch. 30.6.
heel. (m-14) Or 'rush [on them] at the end.' Paronomasia; Gad gedud yegudennu; Gad and troops.
bough; (a-5) Lit. 'son of a fruitful tree.' branches (b-13) Lit. 'daughters.'
coffin (b-20) Lit. 'ark.' Same word as used for the ark in Ex. 25.10 and elsewhere.
